overview: The Commission found 27 Allmont Street preferably preserved and 18 Wedgmere Road significant, while allowing the demolition of the fire-damaged National Register resource at 3-5 Pleasant Street. The meeting also addressed several demolition applications and provided updates on cemetery restoration and historical survey projects.

items.title: 27 Allmont Street Preferably Preserved Hearing
items.summary: Found the pre-1855 resource preferably preserved and imposed an 18-month demolition delay to explore mitigation or reuse options.

items.title: 18 Wedgmere Road Determination of Significance
items.summary: Determined the 1920s bungalow is significant due to its association with the Stearns estate and its well-maintained architectural form.

items.title: 9 Trout Avenue Determination of Significance
items.summary: Determined the property is not significant because it lacks distinctive architectural features and original detail.

items.title: 85 Morton Avenue Demolition Review
items.summary: Rejected the demolition application because building records show the structure was built in 1967 and is not eligible for historical review.

items.title: 38 Pearl Street Demolition Application
items.summary: Accepted the demolition application and agreed to hold significance and preservation hearings back-to-back next month at the request of the owner.

items.title: 3-5 Pleasant Street Demolition Review
items.summary: Voted to pass on further review of the fire-damaged National Register building, effectively permitting its demolition due to extreme structural loss.

items.title: Site Plan Reviews
items.summary: Offered no comment on the 400 Mystic Avenue showroom project and postponed review of the 280 Mystic Avenue 40B project pending corrected documentation.

items.title: Historical Project and Grant Updates
items.summary: Received updates on administrative delays for Cross Street Cemetery restoration and the successful funding of the Thomas Brooks Park project.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Approved the minutes of the April meeting.
